speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. To help me understand what's going on, can you tell me exactly where you are feeling the pain and how long it has been bothering you?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he have any pain in his left hip when you move his leg, or is the discomfort strictly limited to the knee area? I would also like to examine his hips and knees to check for any range of motion limitations or swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine your left hip now, as pain in the hip can often be felt in the knee. I need to check if moving your hip causes discomfort or limits your range of motion.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does moving his hip, especially inward rotation, reproduce the knee pain or cause him distress? I suspect the issue originates in the hip rather than the knee itself. REQUEST TEST: Hip_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the left hip reveals flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head, findings consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease
